scope: Proposition 7.5 (Tube comparison and retained-region energy) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 86. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix P. Let ϵ ↓ 0 through the family in Section 6, allowing all admissible deeper regularizations and rational isolations. Let Rϵ be the union of the retained regions, obtained by removing the long translation-invariant Y middles. Keep initial Y prefixes of length R0 = Cϵ−1/2, as well as the bounded cutoff strips. For harmonic backgrounds, and also for the product-rule backgrounds of Lemma 7.2 chosen with smaller errors, X T ∥β − λT ωS2 ∥2 L2(T ) + ∥β∥2 L2(rest) = oP(ϵ−1 ), ∥β∥2 2 = OP(ϵ−1 ). (7.11) Here T runs over the bulk tubes, bounded end pieces may be transferred to the rest, and ωS2 is the area form of S2(1/ √ 2). The subscript on the little-o means uniformity over those admissible choices and all parameter faces for the fixed problem. For solutions whose total charge is bounded above, bounded ordinary Y gradient perturbations and additional errors of squared cost o(ϵ−1) give Z Rϵ (|Φ|4 + |F0,+ a |2 + |F0 a |2 ) = oP(ϵ−1 ). (7.12) For each fixed ϵ > 0, the same quantities have a finite bound EP,ϵ independent of all subsequently lengthened rational collars and of the omitted Y lengths, with the error costs bounded. The assertions also hold for the retained main fields of ideal tuples with nonnegative omitted losses.
